part.text:
All 19 tests in `tests/say.rs` pass (including the `#[ignore]`d ones via `--include-ignored`).

The implementation in `src/lib.rs`:

- **`under_hundred`** — spells 0–99: teens come straight from a table, and other values compose `TENS[tens]` with an optional `-ONES[ones]` suffix (e.g. `twenty-two`).
- **`under_thousand`** — spells 0–999 as `<hundreds> hundred <rest>`, omitting the remainder when it's zero (e.g. `one hundred`).
- **`encode(n: u64)`** — splits `n` into base-1000 chunks, skips zero chunks, and joins each chunk with its scale word from `["", "thousand", "million", "billion", "trillion", "quadrillion", "quintillion"]` — which covers the full `u64` range, so the `max_i64` and `max_u64` extension tests pass too.

The type signature `encode(n: u64)` enforces the range at compile time, so the commented-out `-1` test case would not compile, as the exercise notes require.
